game: case study cards tell the story: the ask, what LabForge did, what it found

The case cards were terse figures. Each now reads as four short parts:
- The ask: the request in plain words, plus the goal, room and budget from
  the recording's lab_spec;
- What LabForge did: instruments picked from vendor catalogs, room layout and
  violations, simulation, and how many key claims an independent verifier
  checked;
- What it found: a clear verdict with checked numbers ('Can't be done as
  briefed: about 320/day checked vs 768 asked (42%), and $5.89M against a
  $2M budget. Limiting step: SWING XL' / 'Meets the target: 424/day checked
  vs 300 asked, $1.07M of the $2M budget');
- Why it matters: chosen by outcome, not written per case (learn before
  committing the money; or a costed, checked design plus the tested next
  step, with its synchrotron caveat).
All numbers come from the recordings and summaries. The intro says these are
requests modelled on real pipelines, not customer projects.

Strand D: optional synchrotron beamtime cap in the simulator and verifier (off unless set)

sim: optional synchrotron beamtime cap on external steps (off unless set)

params.beamtime_h_per_day on an external step (a plain number is exact; an
uncertain_number such as confidence "estimated" is drawn per replicate) gives
the step that many beam-seconds a day, topped up at each day boundary. Each
run uses its duration_s of beam after its queue time. Beam is served first come,
first served: a beamline collects one shipment at a time, using what's left
today and then the next days' allocations. Use shows in utilisation as
<step>__beamtime, and over 70% raises an external_queue bottleneck ("uses N% of
the beamtime on offer... caps throughput near X").

The default is unchanged. A design without the param simulates exactly as
